clue.text: Kind of school flag appropriate whilst in transit

parts.note: a high school is a kind of secondary school
a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: A school banner is commandeered somewhere along a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here: to seize a vehicle on its journey; HIGHJACK is a variant spelling of hijack.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize control of a vehicle, plane or cargo during its journey.

clue.text: Limp round without Bob in an unattractive place

indicators.note: the shortened name is placed inside the word for a dreary spot

parts.note: a hole is a dismal, unpleasant place to live

indicators.note: the round letter is taken away from the name, leaving its other letters

parts.note: the name taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone limps around a grim spot now that Bob has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like the haircut or a curtsey, but it is the name; 'without' removes O, the round letter, and 'in' places what is left inside the dismal place.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to walk awkwardly, favouring a sore leg.

clue.text: Complains if Nora's around after midnight

indicators.note: the jumbled name follows the middle letter, so it comes second

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G

indicators.note: the letters of the name are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the name with its S, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles when Nora is still about in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the very middle of the word night, not the hour; 'around' rearranges Nora's letters, which come 'after' that middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Groans are moaning complaints, so someone who groans is grumbling.

clue.text: Jules pointlessly gets doctor in muddle

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the shortened name
a compass point, south, is dropped from the name

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Jules, confused, calls the doctor over his muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' drops S (south, a compass point) from JULES to leave JULE; MB goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble is a disordered heap or mess.

clue.text: Undertaker caught taking farm vehicle

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on means taking, as in being on medication
a tractor pulls machinery on a farm

explanation.surface: A funeral director is arrested while driving a tractor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaker' is not the funeral sense: it is one who undertakes a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor undertakes to do work for an agreed price.

clue.text: Pet firm. Southern group

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Notes about an animal-care firm and a band from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is a verb: to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to pamper or indulge them.

clue.text: So stands around helping to — make deliveries

indicators.note: the reversed little word goes round the portion
in a down clue, standing up means reading the word upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ration is a helping or allotted portion

explanation.surface: Someone stands about helping to hand out deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'stands' means read upwards, so So becomes OS, which goes 'around' the helping; the dash is only a line break on the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeches are delivered, so formal addresses are deliveries.

clue.text: Boxer was out but arranged to accept finance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the finance letters into their middle
the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: HP, hire purchase, is a form of finance

explanation.surface: A boxer who had been knocked out fixed up some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' could be a dog, but a southpaw is a left-handed fighter; 'arranged' turns the letters of 'was out' into SOUTAW, and 'to accept' puts the finance letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed fighter in the ring.

clue.text: Allow to alter wrong note

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a wrong, jumbled order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An instruction to let someone correct a wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges TOALTER into TOLERAT, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to put up with it.

clue.text: Bulb started taking shape and flowering

indicators.note: the start of the word bulb gives its first letter

parts.note: looming means emerging into view, taking shape

explanation.surface: A bulb begins to sprout and comes into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulb and flowering share a garden picture, but 'Bulb started' gives only B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooming means producing flowers.

clue.text: Part-time worker from America retired in California

indicators.note: the reversed country goes inside the state abbreviation
retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A temp from the States has retired to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns USA into ASU, which goes 'in' CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual is a worker employed irregularly rather than full time.

clue.text: Publican has to come down and look, by the way

parts.note: to land is to come down to earth
lo is an old word for look
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A pub owner must come downstairs and peer down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord keeps a pub in Britain.

clue.text: Where endless sex appeal is in decline

indicators.note: the appeal letters are placed inside the shortened word
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: it is an old slang term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A question about where allure goes as it fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the E off WHERE, leaving WHER; IT 'is in' that.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to fade or shrivel, losing vigour.

clue.text: Cold during Easter rings meteorologist

parts.note: for means during, as in for a week

indicators.note: the festival's letters surround the cold letter

parts.note: taken as written
C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cold snap over Easter calls for a weatherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' is a verb: the festival surrounds the cold letter, giving ECASTER, and 'during' supplies the opening letters by the sense 'for the length of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecaster is a meteorologist predicting conditions.

clue.text: Person doing a balancing act?

parts.note: not a circus performer but someone who balances books of figures

explanation.definitionFit: Accountancy involves balancing ledgers so that debits match credits.

clue.text: Taking back cover off notice bloomer

indicators.note: the whole run of words is read back to front

parts.note: a lid is a cover
taken as written
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: Removing a cover after receiving notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking back' reverses LIDOFFAD to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is a flower, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Disagreeably assertive step by conservationists

parts.note: a stride is a long step
the NT, National Trust, conserves British historic places

explanation.surface: Conservation campaigners take a pushy step.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud, harsh and forceful in manner.

clue.text: Divine broadcast free to students

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A free radio programme for students about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb, to foresee; 'broadcast' turns the letters of 'free to' into FORETE, and L for learner is doubled for students.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict the future by insight.

clue.text: Star-gazer found no star more confusing

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up, confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A skywatcher finds that the sky has fewer stars and is puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges NOSTARMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies stars and planets.

clue.text: Intense fire ruined engineer

indicators.note: the word is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: A fierce blaze has wrecked the engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges FIRE into FIER, then CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means violent or intense in force.

clue.text: Powerful company gent

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mighty businessman from the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and persuasive.

clue.text: Officer said to be a bit of a nut!

indicators.note: the officer's title is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: An officer is reputed to be rather mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nut' reads as a bit crazy, but it is the edible part of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel is the soft edible part inside a nutshell.

clue.text: First class bolted outside and didn't pass

indicators.note: the word for ran off goes outside the first-class letters

parts.note: fled means ran away, bolted
A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: A top student ran out and flunked.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as AI, the digit one doing duty as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail an exam is not to pass it.

clue.text: I'm to account for returning exclusive jacket

indicators.note: the two pieces before it are read back to front

parts.note: taken without its apostrophe
sole means exclusive, as in sole rights

explanation.surface: Someone must explain bringing back a designer jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses IMAC to CAMI, then SOLE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole was once a short sleeved jacket, now an under-bodice.

clue.text: See warped cover put back over fuel

indicators.note: the reversed lid goes over, outside, the jumbled letters
the word for a cover is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A warped lid is put back over a fuel tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped' turns SEE into ESE; 'put back' turns LID into DIL, which goes 'over' ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy oil burned in engines.

clue.text: Way one rug is damaged by swimmer

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A fish swims past and damages a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is any fish here; 'is damaged' turns the letters of 'one rug' into URGEON, after the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, famous for caviar.

clue.text: Rarely illuminated club abandoned fight

parts.note: lit means illuminated

indicators.note: the club is dropped from the word for fight

parts.note: a battle is a fight
a bat is a club used in cricket

explanation.surface: A rarely lit club gave up on a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTLE 'abandoned' BAT, leaving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Little as an adverb means hardly ever, as in 'little seen'.

clue.text: Note in Latin or badly written Chinese?

indicators.note: the note sits inside the rearranged letters
badly written letters are garbled into a new order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Is that scrawl Latin or Chinese?
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly written' rearranges LATINOR into ORINTAL; E goes 'in' it. The question mark shows Chinese is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is one example of something from the Far East.
